specification.title: The connection is terminated inside a nested scope that then fails
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Write the marker `outer`, and make sure the write was sent.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure the write was sent.
Checkpoint `inner-after-write`: report the backend PID. The runner sees the savepoint's subtransaction lock. The runner then terminates the backend, and waits until it has gone.
Wait settle_ms, then raise an application error in the nested scope; its ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails on the closed connection.
The outer scope catches the nested scope's error.
Checkpoint `after-outer`, after the outer transaction's API has returned: report the same backend PID. The runner records whether that session is still inside a transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If the API reports that the outer transaction committed, PostgreSQL committed it, with the outer scope's writes and none of the failed nested scope's writes.
When the outer transaction's API has returned, the connection that ran it is no longer inside a transaction.

execution.description: Connection::transaction(Closure) on one Capsule connection. Nested transaction() is a savepoint named transN. Eloquent creates write the markers. DatabaseTransactionsManager is not set. PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT is false. There is no pool.

configuration.nested: savepoint transN on the same connection
configuration.transactions_manager: not set; Capsule does not install DatabaseTransactionsManager
configuration.pool: none; one connection on the Capsule manager
configuration.isolation: connection config isolation_level, applied by PostgresConnector when set; transaction() takes no isolation argument
configuration.command_tag: not read; PDO::commit() does not expose one

execution.form: Managed Connection::transaction(Closure). Nested transaction() is a savepoint. Writes are Eloquent creates. The persistent mode is the same callback with PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend(pid), run by the runner from its own connection.
fault.injection_point: Inside the nested scope, after its write, before the framework's savepoint rollback.
fault.preconditions: The PID the adapter reports belongs to the case's database.
fault.expected_server: The backend exits, and the whole transaction is rolled back.
fault.expected_client: Connection errors for the savepoint rollback and for anything after it.

knowledge: The framework sees its connection fail during the savepoint rollback.

api_outcome.basis: Connection::transaction() returned. When the callback returns, Laravel calls PDO::commit() if the transaction level is 1. The return value of PDO::commit() is not inspected.
api_outcome.contract: Laravel 13.38.0 Illuminate\Database\Connection::transaction() (ManagesTransactions) begins a transaction, runs the callback, and on return calls getPdo()->commit() when $this->transactions === 1. A thrown callback calls rollBack() and rethrows, unless the exception is a concurrency error and attempts remain. The default attempts value is 1. Connection::commit() calls getPdo()->commit() only when transactionLevel() === 1. A nested commit decrements the counter and does not send RELEASE SAVEPOINT. Connection::beginTransaction() at level 0 calls PDO::beginTransaction(). At level 1 or more it execs SAVEPOINT transN (Grammar::compileSavepoint). rollBack() to level 0 calls PDO::rollBack() when PDO::inTransaction() is true. A nested rollBack execs ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT transN (Grammar::compileSavepointRollBack). Neither commit() nor transaction() reads PDO::errorInfo() or a PostgreSQL command tag after commit(). executeBeginTransactionStatement() is getPdo()->beginTransaction() only. It takes no isolation argument. PostgresConnector::configureIsolationLevel runs "set session characteristics as transaction isolation level {$config['isolation_level']}" when the connection is opened, if that config key is set. This adapter does not set DatabaseTransactionsManager. Capsule does not set it either, so afterCommit() is not called on this path.

error.message: SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 7 FATAL: terminating connection due to administrator command server closed the connection unexpectedly This probably means the server terminated abnormally before or while processing the request.

evaluation.reason: TX-02.1 violated: the API reported: committed; xid 17858 rolled back at report time (`after-outer`); outer visible: false; inner (failed scope) visible: false

preconditions.description: the write of marker "outer" had reached PostgreSQL at `outer-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "inner" had reached PostgreSQL at `inner-after-write` (a subtransaction lock, in pg_locks)
the runner terminated the backend at `inner-after-write`, and it had gone before the adapter resumed
the nested scope's error reached the outer scope, which handled it
the runner observed the transaction's session after the outer API returned
